note: The recession-forecast record comes from one paper, quoted at its own numbers. `predicted` counts recessions that the private-sector consensus (Consensus Economics) had forecast by the April of the year BEFORE the recession began — the paper's own headline test.
source: Zidong An, João Tovar Jalles and Prakash Loungani, "How Well Do Economists Forecast Recessions?", IMF Working Paper WP/18/39, March 2018. Nate Silver's 2008 and 2012 results are the published FiveThirtyEight record. The Samuelson line is from his Newsweek column, 19 September 1966.

quote.text: Wall Street indexes predicted nine out of the last five recessions!
quote.misquote: Economists have predicted nine of the last five recessions.
